Subject: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls & routing / CloudScale

Hi Samantha / Marc —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and the items we agreed to follow up on. Please reply with corrections if I missed anything.

Pain points / impetus:
- Current system enforces tenant limits at the application layer; this is becoming brittle as you onboard more partners.
- Need clearer tiering so that enterprise customers get different routing/throughput guarantees and lower latency.
- Billing team needs an auditable per-tenant quota/reporting mechanism (daily usage + burst allowance).

Current stack you shared:
- AWS (us-east-1 primary), custom API gateway in front of service, Redis for short-term caches, Postgres for metering
- Model/service calls flow through a central pool today (no per-tenant routing)

Success criteria (what success looks like to you):
- Ability to assign tenants to tiers (free / standard / premium) with per-tenant rate limits and quotas
- Route premium tenants to dedicated or higher-priority pools to meet p50 latency < 300ms under typical load
- Per-tenant daily usage reporting and export for billing automation
- Support for burst windows (short bursts above quota for trusted tenants)

Open questions / clarifications we discussed:
- Expected peak QPS per top tenant: ~250-300 QPS during peaks (you confirmed top 5 tenants drive ~60% of load)
- Desired strictness of enforcement: soft quota + alerts for standard, hard quota for free tier, guaranteed throughput for premium
- Any regulatory constraints for tenant-level data isolation: none beyond standard SOC2 requirements (you will send any checklist if needed)

Next steps (agreed):
1) I will share a short spec showing how Redwood handles per-tenant quotas, routing policies, and tiering — includes a sample rate-limit table and routing fallback behavior.
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive (Engineering + Networking) with Lauren to demo routing controls and latency profiles.
3) Marissa will pull together pricing scenarios once we confirm the target throughput assumptions.

Tentative timing: deep-dive next week (Mar 9-11) — let me know best times.

Thanks — I’ll attach the spec and our security brief in the next message.

Ben Carter

Thanks Ben — this looks good and captures the main points. A couple of additions/answers from our side: 

- Peak per-tenant QPS: top 1–2 enterprise customers can spike to ~400 QPS for short periods (10–15 minutes). The rest are <100 QPS.
- We’d like premium tenants to have both routing priority and the option to pin to a dedicated pool (customer-managed or Redwood-dedicated).
- Billing: we do hourly metering but bill monthly. We need CSV export of per-tenant usage with invoice-ready columns.
- Burst policy idea: allow a short grace window (couple minutes) where a premium tenant can exceed quota by up to 2x, but that is chargeable and tracked.

Regulatory: we don’t have additional constraints beyond SOC2; our security team may ask for more detailed docs (I can loop them in if useful).

We’d like the deep-dive focused on: routing policy examples (how to map tenant -> pool), enforcement semantics (soft vs. hard limits), and demo of the usage export.

Availability for next week is mostly Wed/Thu morning PT.

—Sam
